chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Qasim from Aban from Mansur ibn Hazim who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the young girl (bint mahd) in whom pregnancy is not feared, he said: 'There is no waiting period (iddah) upon her.'

key_terms.الْجَارِيَة: The young girl (bint mahd), specifically one who has not yet menstruated or is not expected to.
key_terms.الْعِدَّة: The waiting period a woman must observe after divorce or death of husband before remarrying.

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (Iddah) for a young girl who has not yet reached puberty or menstruated?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a young girl (bint mahd) who is not expected to conceive is exempt from the four-month-and-ten-day waiting period prescribed for pregnant widows, as the primary rationale for the extended iddah—ensuring lineage purity—is absent. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that legal obligations are contingent upon physiological capability, distinguishing her status from that of a mature woman or a pregnant widow. It underscores the flexibility of Islamic family law in accommodating natural developmental stages.
